passage.title: The Quiet Qualities (extract)
paras: We often confuse leaders with the loudest people in the room. Yet history suggests that great leaders share three quieter qualities. The first is integrity: people follow those whose words and actions match. The second is humility: a leader who listens makes fewer fatal mistakes. The third is accountability: the best leaders accept that power must answer to someone.
Consider the captain who is last to leave a sinking ship. Nobody elected her for her speeches. They trust her because she puts the crew first.

Charisma has its uses. A confident voice can calm a frightened crowd, and a stirring speech can make people brave. But charisma without integrity is dangerous. History is full of persuasive speakers who led their followers into disaster, because nobody dared to ask whether the words were true.
